title: feat(post): the document's program number and comment, per dialect (#258 part 2)
body:
Part 2 of #258's split: the program number and comment. Today every post hard-codes `O0001` followed by the machine name. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0.

## What changed
- **Document field:** a new `ProgramInfo { number, comment }` singleton (schema.rs). Unset means every post writes exactly what it wrote before.
- **Command:** an undoable `SetProgramInfo`. At creation it refuses by name:
  - a number outside 1-9999;
  - a comment over 40 characters, non-printable or non-ASCII, or containing `( ) % ; *`.

  Chosen: refuse rather than sanitise. Heidenhain and SINUMERIK, which use the comment as the program name, check it against their name rules at post time.
- **UI:** "Program number" and "Program comment" fields on the Post page. They commit on Enter or when focus leaves.
- **MCP:** a new `set_program` tool.
- **Scripts:** they get a `program` global `{number, numbered, comment}` (`engine::run_program_with`); `programNumber` is kept. Documented in docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md.
- **Per-operation files:** one file per op counts up from the stated number and is refused past O9999. The old code silently clamped instead.
- **Project file v59:** an optional `program` key. This is a version step, not just an added key, because an older build would drop the key and post O0001, which could overwrite a different program on the control. v58 files load with nothing set.

**Per dialect.** Each rule is cited in its .cps. The manual section references were written from memory, so a maintainer may want to check them against the manuals.
- **Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak:** `O####` (O0001-O9999), then `(<comment or machine name>)`.
- **Haas:** five-digit `O#####`, written only when a number is set.
- **Tormach PathPilot:** never an O-word, because LinuxCNC's O words are subroutine and flow-control words. A number goes in the header comment.
- **Heidenhain ISO:** the comment becomes the program name, `%<name> G71 *`, limited to file-name characters. If only a number is set, it is used as the name.
- **SINUMERIK:** the comment becomes `%_N_<NAME>_MPF` (letters, digits and `_`; the first two are letters or `_` plus a letter; at most 24 characters). A name that breaks these rules is refused, not renamed. The number goes in a `; PROGRAM n` comment.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/258-program-number.md`.

## How tested
- **New `program_info` tests (9):**
  - output is byte-identical in all 7 posts when nothing is set;
  - each dialect's header with a number and comment, and with a number alone;
  - post-time refusals;
  - command validation, undo and redo;
  - the typed-number parser (accepts `O0012`);
  - per-op numbering;
  - a live post writes `O0077 (Lid)`, and undo restores O0001;
  - round-trip: a v58 file loads with nothing set, and a corrupt value is refused.
- **Also new:** `mcp_setup::set_program_states_undoes_and_refuses_by_name`, and ui `program_info_tests` (typing into the fields, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y, a refusal).
- **Gate:** 35 app test binaries (338 tests) pass, including conformance, golden_cl, posting, every post suite, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, mcp and mcp_setup. All camcraft-post tests pass. ui lib passes 378; the one failure is the headless-GPU test, which also fails on this machine without the change. Clippy (post/app/ui, `-D warnings`) is clean. **No golden changed.**

## Not exercised
A GUI hands-on check, and a run of a numbered program on a control or in the Hub. G-code changes only when a number or comment is set.

Changelog: The document states its program number and comment (Post page, MCP set_program); each post writes it in its own dialect - O-word (Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak, Haas), Heidenhain program name, SINUMERIK %_N_..._MPF, PathPilot header comment; project v59 (#258)

Refs #258

title: fix(sim): credit an edge-break record only within its op's stated width
body:
**Stacked on #502** (chamfer/deburr edge breaks). Its commits show here until #502 merges; this PR adds one commit on top.

## What changed

The program sim forgave convicted columns down to a cached edge-break record's depth. The record is file data, so a hand-edited or corrupted project could state any depth and hide a real gouge under an inflated bevel (review note on #502). Each op's records are now held to the break width its own params state: `Chamfer2D` / `Deburr` `width`, against the record's `depth / slope`, with a micron of lattice slack. A wider record, or a record on a kind that declares no break, is dropped with a logged warning, and its columns are judged against the sharp model: stricter, never looser. The bound sits where the sim reads each op's records (`stock_sim::breaks::bounded`), so a fresh generation and a loaded file are judged alike.

## How tested

- New `edge_break_bound`, 3/3:
  - `an_inflated_record_no_longer_forgives_a_deeper_cut`: a chamfer ridden 0.3 mm deep, saved, its break depth hand-scaled ×5 in the file and reloaded. It still convicts.
  - `an_unedited_file_still_credits_its_own_break`
  - `the_bound_reads_the_ops_own_width`
- With the call site reverted, the first test fails ("the inflated record forgave a real gouge"). That is the bug.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`, escalated to batch, 906 s: every crate suite is green, including #502's `edge_break_gate`, `deburr_links` and every stock_sim-mapped suite. Clippy `-D warnings` is clean on all 8 crates. ui: only the three known GPU-adapter reds that are also red on main.

## Not exercised

A GUI view. The change only narrows what the verify credits.

Changelog: The gouge check credits a chamfer's or deburr's declared edge break only within the width the operation states, so a hand-edited project cannot widen it (#529)

Fixes #529

title: fix(post): a touch probe section starts no spindle on any mill post
body:
## What changed

A touch probe is never spun (#523). Haas, Tormach, Sinumerik, Heidenhain and Mazak posted `S<rpm> M3` (Mazak `MOTON S…`) for every section, a probe's S0 included. Each now gates its spindle start on `sRpm > 0`, the rule `fanuc.cps` has used since #108. Heidenhain also drops the `S` word from its `TOOL CALL` at rpm 0.

- No extra `M5` is needed: every post already ends each section with `M5`, so a probe section never inherits a running spindle.
- A cutter can never lose its spindle through this: `Tool::is_sane` refuses rpm 0 on every tool, so S0 reaches a post only from a probe dump.
- **Reachability:** on main, only Fanuc posts probe moves, and it was already gated. PR #500 (Tormach probe positioning) makes the Tormach path reachable, which is where `S0 M3` showed up in the Hub run. #500 should merge after this.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/probe_spindle.rs`:
- `a_section_with_no_spindle_speed_starts_no_spindle_on_any_mill_post`: an rpm-0 section through all six mill posts posts no `S` word and no `M3`/`M03`/`MOTON`. It fails without the post changes (`haas: a probe section posts ["S0", "M3"]`).
- `a_cutting_section_still_starts_its_spindle_on_every_mill_post`: an 8000 rpm section still posts its `S` word and spindle start on all six.

`scripts/gate.sh quick`, which escalated to batch, ran 782 s. Results:
- geometry, cl, tools, post, sim and motion: green.
- app: green, 1433 passed and 0 failed across all binaries, conformance and every NC golden byte-exact.
- clippy `-D warnings` on all 8 crates: green.
- ui: the only red is the five known failures that are also red on main: the three headless tests that need a GPU adapter, and `structural::shell_structure_dark/light` (the `v0.0.0` label).

## Not exercised

No Hub run. No posted program on main reaches the changed path except through Fanuc, which is unchanged. Cutting output is byte-identical, since every golden is unchanged.

Changelog: A probing section no longer starts the spindle (S0 M3) on the Haas, Tormach, Siemens, Heidenhain and Mazak posts (#523)

Fixes #523

title: feat(turning): optional repeat pass at each threading depth
body:
**Replaces #437** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #433** (#417), which is on #432 (#416). Part of #363. The #418 work is bf3b0d58.

## What changed
- **The option:** `ThreadInfeed.repeat_each_depth`, off by default. Every pass above the root is followed by an identical copy: same tip depth, same lattice shift, same helix phase. So a repeat can never cut deeper or move. The finishing and spring passes at the root are not repeated.
- **Alternating infeed:** the side flips once per depth, not per cut, so a repeat keeps its flank.
- **G76 refuses it by name.** The record carries a `repeat_each_depth` flag, written to the stream as `REP 1` only when set, plus a `RepeatEachDepth` post property. `fanuc-lathe.cps` refuses with "repeat each roughing depth is not a G76 cycle (the cycle cuts each depth once)".
- **Defaults are byte-identical:** the stamp adds one byte only when the flag is on, and no project key or stream word is written when it's off. No version rung.
- **UI:** a "Repeat each depth" checkbox on the Passes tab, after Spring passes. Its tooltip says G32 only, that G76 refuses it, and that tooling makers recommend against routine spring passes.
- `docs/decisions/418-thread-repeat-pass.md`

## How tested
- motion `turning_thread_infeed`, 10/10, including two new tests:
  - every roughing depth is cut twice (0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 0.8, 1.1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.2) and the default is unchanged move for move;
  - a repeat is the same pass under every method × schedule, and the verdict stays silent.
- app:
  - `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5: the toggle goes stale and back to OK, takes 3 then 5 plunges, with undo and redo; round-trip writes the key only when set;
  - `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 5/5: G76 refuses the repeat; `REP 1` rides the stream; G32 posts 5 passes.
- `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `inverted_post`, `project_roundtrip` and the app lib pass. No golden changed.
- `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on cl, post, motion, app and ui is clean.
- The only failure is the headless-GPU ui test (no adapter on this Mac).

## Not exercised (draft)
GUI check and a lathe sim or machine run. There is a combined test kit for #416, #417 and #418.

Changelog: Threading op: optional repeat of each roughing depth (G32 output; G76 refuses it by name) (#418)

Fixes #418

title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.**
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It's not a gouge, but it isn't what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: exactly the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That isn't so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm;
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- Existing post, cl, inverted_post, lathe_post, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, tool_law, tool_gate and commands_undo suites are green.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` (cl, post, motion, app, ui) is clean.
- The gate escalated to batch (cl changed). It fails only on tests already red on main: headless GPU, #415, and `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised / not confirmed by sources (draft until a lathe sim or machine run)
1. Which way Fanuc shifts Z per pass for flank infeed. This follows LinuxCNC's sign; either sign is gouge-safe.
2. Whether the control also shifts each pass's end Z. If not, early passes end up to k·tan θ off at the runout, shallower than the root.
3. How the minimum-depth clamp applies (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition).
4. Micron rounding of the words: the control's ladder can differ by under 1 µm.

None of these moves the finished thread form.

Changelog: G76 threading output states the passes that were verified: the finish allowance R is posted (default threads now post R0.4 instead of R0), and options G76 cannot express are refused by name (#417)

Fixes #417

title: feat(turning): threading infeed method and decreasing-depth pass schedule
body:
**Replaces #432** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

Part of #363 (peck threading; the research comment there has the sources). Follow-up #417 (PR stacked on this one) makes the G76 output match these passes.

## What changed
**New threading op param `infeed_plan` (`turning::ThreadInfeed`).**
- **Infeed method:** radial, modified flank at an angle θ, or alternating flank.
- **Depth schedule:** constant depth, or constant area (first depth × √n).
- **Minimum depth per pass, finish allowance, and spring passes** (default 0, capped at 98).
- The existing `infeed` is the first-pass depth.
- It's shown as rows on the op's Passes tab (`thread_infeed_page.rs`).

**Kernel.** `crates/motion/src/turning/infeed.rs` lays the passes from the plan. `thread_in` calls `thread_planned_in` with the default plan.
- **Flank:** each pass starts shifted by −(tip − root)·tan θ along its travel. Finishing and spring passes sit on the pitch lattice, so lead and spindle phase never change.
- **Safety:** every pass stays inside the finished V exactly when θ ≤ half the insert's included angle. A larger angle is refused by name at the command (create, paste, edit, retype via `thread_gate`) and again at Generate.
- **Alternating:** flips the side each pass.

**The verdict judges the laid passes.** `the_verdict_reads_the_shifted_pass` pins a past-half-angle pass being convicted. `attach_cycle` moved to `thread_cycle.rs`.

**Defaults are byte-identical.** The default plan makes the same `blade::rungs(root, ref_top, infeed, 0)` call at the same stations.
- The op stamp includes the plan only when it isn't the default, so cached threads stay fresh.
- The project key is written only when non-default, so there's no version rung. An older build drops a non-default plan and cuts the radial ladder; that's not a gouge.
- No existing golden changed.

`docs/decisions/416-thread-infeed.md`

## How tested
- New motion `turning_thread_infeed` (8 tests):
  - √n depths with the minimum-depth clamp;
  - allowance plus spring-pass count;
  - flank shift, including the full 30°;
  - alternating flip;
  - verdict silent for every method × schedule on the thread fixture;
  - a shifted pass is convicted;
  - refusals by name.
- New app `turning_thread_infeed` (4/4, plus 1 after the merge): the plan runs in a document; refusals at create and edit; undo/redo (op goes stale); project round-trip with no key for the default plan.
- Existing suites unchanged and green: motion `turning_thread` and `turning_thread_cycle`; app `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_field_tools` and `project_roundtrip`.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` passes except tests that already fail on main:
  - the headless-GPU ui tests;
  - `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` (#415);
  - `swarf_pose_continuity` (2 tests; red on main, fixed by PR #351).

## Not exercised (draft)
- GUI check of the new Passes-tab rows.
- **Posted G-code for non-default plans** (flank, constant area, allowance, spring passes) is new. It needs a lathe simulator or machine run before ready. Default plans post exactly as before.

Changelog: Threading op: infeed method (radial / modified flank / alternating), decreasing-depth schedule, minimum depth, finish allowance and spring passes (#416)

Fixes #416

title: feat(setup): per-setup post options and the setup's own tool-list export
body:
> Replaces #423, moved to the new fork (the old fork left NeoTech's network, and a push there closes the PR). Main is merged in. The two conflicts were module lists in `ui/src/state.rs` and `egui_app/tests.rs`, where both sides are kept (#371's tool_body). `setup_post_options` passes 8/8, the ui lib tests 11/11, and clippy for app and ui is clean. Still a draft, waiting on the hands-on GUI check (rebuilt `camcraft-ui-423`).

## What changed
**Post options per setup** (same own / follow-the-document law #343 gave the post itself):
- `SetupDef.post_options: Option<PostOptions>`; `None` follows the document (every older file and every new setup).
- New undoable command `SetSetupPostOptions`; a no-op request is refused by name. A datum transfer copies the source setup's options with its post.
- `posting::post_options` returns the active setup's own options, else the document's (mirrors `post_of`). "Skip pauses and homes" is read per operation from that op's setup, so one setup can skip its stops while another keeps them. Output (one file per op) and thread output are program-wide: setups that disagree are refused by name, next to #343's one-mount check.
- Project file: an additive setup key `post_options` (`{"threading":"g32"|"g76","skip_stops":..,"per_op_files":..}`), omitted when `None`; no version step (stays v57), so a document that never sets it saves byte-identically. An unknown threading word is a corrupt-file refusal naming the setup.
- UI: the setup's **Post** page ends with a "Post options" group - radios "Use the document's post options" / "This setup has its own post options" and a note saying whose options the widgets above edit. The existing option widgets route to the active setup's own options when it has them.

**Setup tool-list export**
- `app::tool_list_export` (pure read): rows in first-use order from `tool_list::for_setup` - T number, name, diameter (mm), kind, holder (`D x L` or `none`), ops using it. `.csv` -> RFC 4180 CSV (CRLF, quoted fields); any other extension -> fixed-column text.
- The setup's **Tool list** page gets an "Export tool list…" button (save dialog, CSV/Text filters, default `<Setup>-tools.csv`). A command-free file write like the setup sheet: nothing enters the history.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (all camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1725 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main: `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` (#415) and the GPU headless trio (`headless_run_succeeds`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`, `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`). Goldens (`golden_cl` 23, posts) and `project_roundtrip` (69) unchanged. Clippy `-D warnings` clean on app + ui.

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/setup_post_options.rs`: `a_setups_own_post_options_do_undo_redo`, `a_setup_that_skips_posts_without_its_stops_while_the_other_follows_the_document`, `setups_disagreeing_on_the_output_are_refused_by_name`, `a_single_setup_document_posts_byte_identically`, `own_post_options_round_trip_and_old_files_follow_the_document`, `a_datum_transfer_keeps_the_source_setups_post_options`, `the_tool_list_exports_as_csv_and_text`, `a_tool_list_field_with_a_comma_is_quoted`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::setup_post_options`: `the_option_switches_land_on_the_active_setups_own_options`, `the_post_page_radio_gives_the_setup_its_own_options`, `the_tool_list_page_exports_the_setups_tools`.

## Not exercised
The real rfd save dialog (tests write through `ToolListExportFile`); a per-setup G76 thread post end to end on Fanuc Lathe; one-file-per-op from a setup's own options (same `post_options` path `per_op_files` already covers). No hand GUI check yet - **draft until the GUI check**.

Posted G-code: existing documents post byte-identically; output only differs for a setup that is given its own options.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/389-setup-tool-list.md`.

Changelog: A setup can carry its own post options (skip pauses and homes, output, thread output) or follow the document's; the setup's Tool list page exports its tools as CSV or text

Fixes #389

title: fix(app): a saved machine file keeps its key order
body:
**Stacked on #478** (#383, the Machines pane edits and saves `.mch` files). The #480 work is a95093c0.

## What changed
A `.mch` saved from the Machines pane keeps the key order it was read in. Keys the file didn't have go at the end of their object. Project files are untouched.

- **New `crates/app/src/machine/order.rs`** (with provenance).
  - It reads the source text once and records the key order of every object and array as a `KeyOrder` tree. A duplicated key keeps its first position and takes its last value, like `serde_json::Value`.
  - `to_pretty(value, order)` writes the same layout as `to_string_pretty` (2-space indent, `": "`), with keys in the recorded order, then any unknown keys sorted.
- **`MachineDraft`** gains `order: KeyOrder`. `open` and `from_template` fill it from the source, `blank` leaves it empty, and `text()` writes through `to_pretty`. Edits still act on the plain `serde_json::Value`, so `fields.rs` is unchanged.
- **No new dependency, and `serde_json/preserve_order` is not turned on workspace-wide.** That would change every JSON writer, project files included. `indexmap` is already in the lock file, but using it directly would still be a dependency change, and the order visitor is about 60 lines.
- The `docs/decisions/383-machines-edit.md` "key order" entry is replaced by this decision.

## How tested
- `machine_edit::a_saved_file_keeps_its_key_order_and_new_keys_go_last`: a hand-written file in deliberately unsorted order, with unknown keys, gets an edit plus a new `spindle`/`max_speed` block. The saved file's exact key list is checked.
- `machine_edit::a_new_machine_writes_the_same_text_serde_json_would`: with no recorded order, the output matches `to_string_pretty` byte for byte.
- `machine_edit`, `machine_library`, `machine` and `project_roundtrip` (69) pass. Project files are byte-identical; no project writer changed.
- `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Limitation
Only the key order is kept. A hand-written file's inline arrays (e.g. `[0, 0, 1]` on one line) still come out multi-line.

Changelog: A machine file saved from the Machines pane keeps its key order (new keys go last) (#480)

Fixes #480

title: feat(app): raise fixture-striking links and retracts over the steel
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 5 of #339 per the triage on the issue: link and retract routing around fixtures.

## What changed
New `crates/app/src/operation/fixture_route.rs`, with one hook in `generate.rs` before the verify pass. It runs for upright mill paths only.

**The rule:**
- **What a link is:** the longest run of straight rapids between two non-rapid moves, or a path end.
- **When it counts as struck:** the gate's own fixture laws flag it. That's #464's whole-stack law (d2) plus #476's mesh acquittal, so a routed link is judged exactly as the post gate will judge it.
- **The fix:** a struck link becomes three G0 moves: up at its start XY, across, down to its end. The height is the higher of the link's own top and the highest box top under the traverse plus 5 mm (`ROUTE_GAP`). "Under the traverse" means every box the widest band reaches along the XY segment.
- **The cap:** the machine's stated Z stroke (WCS origin Z plus the top of the stroke), keeping at least 0.5 mm over the steel. Steel taller than that **refuses generation by name**: "the link at moves i..j … cannot clear fixture 'Clamp1': its steel stands to Z …, and the machine's Z stroke tops out at Z …". With no stroke stated there is no cap, as everywhere else.
- **Re-judging:** the re-laid link is judged again. If it's still struck, the steel stands over the link's own end column and no height helps. The link is then left as laid, its `FixtureHit` still blocks the post by name, and a path note says why.
- **Notes:** every raised link gets a path note: how many rose, from where, over which fixture, to what Z.

**Left as today (report-only):**
- **Keep-down feed links.** In the CL stream they look exactly like cuts, so lifting one could silently skip a cut. They're only taken inside the cut area, so if one hits steel the cuts beside it hit too, and the post is refused anyway. A keep-down **rapid** run at depth does become retract, traverse and plunge.
- **Other paths:** posed and rotary paths, lathe tools, paths with canned cycles (a traverse inserted between holes could post as a drill), thread or probe records, and runs inside a compensated span.

**Posted G-code changes only** for documents with a link the fixture laws strike, and only those links' G0 moves. Documents without fixtures return early untouched, and links that already clear are never rewritten, so all goldens are unchanged.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-routing.md`

## How tested
- **New app `fixture_route`** (6 tests):
  - A Contour around two blocks with a strap clamp to Z 40 between them, at clearance 25. As generated, the gate refuses ("strikes a fixture"). After the fix, the links rise to Z 45, the post is clean, the cuts are identical, and the note names Clamp1.
  - A clamp the links already clear leaves the path byte for byte.
  - A 100 mm Z stroke still routes over the 40 mm clamp, while a 400 mm clamp refuses generation naming 'Clamp1' and "Z 400.000".
  - A stay-down rapid link becomes retract, traverse and plunge. Clear steel and no steel are untouched.
  - Steel over a link's own end is left as laid and said.
  - A ceiling under the steel refuses, and a ceiling over it caps the rise.
- **Existing suites keep their verdicts:** fixtures (14), fixture_mesh (3), fixture_law_gaps (3), posting (17), tool_body (8). All app test binaries passed in the quick gate.
- `clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
This changes posted G-code (raised G0 links) for documents with struck fixtures, so it's a draft until a Hub or machine run. It needs a project with a clamp between features.

Changelog: Links and retracts that would strike a fixture are raised over the steel (a clamp taller than the machine's Z stroke refuses generation by name) instead of only being reported (#339)

Refs #339

title: feat(mcp): serve the MCP tool table live from inside the GUI
body:
> Replaces #428, moved to the new fork (the old one left NeoTech's network; a push there closes the PR). Main is merged in; the one conflict was the module list in `mcp/mod.rs`, where both sides are kept. `mcp` 9/9, `mcp_live` 6/6 and `mcp_pick` 2/2 pass, and clippy for app and ui is clean. Still a draft, waiting on the hands-on GUI check (refreshed binaries `camcraft-ui-428` and `camcraft-cli-428`).

## What changed
The GUI can host the same MCP tool table (`app::mcp`) live, so an agent drives the open document and the user watches it in the viewport.

- **Opt-in, loopback only.** Off by default; started with `--mcp-port <n>` / `--mcp-port=<n>` or `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT` (flag wins; `0` picks a free port). Binds 127.0.0.1. A bad value exits 2.
- **Transport:** plain TCP carrying the same newline-delimited JSON-RPC as `camcraft-cli mcp`, plus a stdio<->TCP bridge `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` so stdio MCP clients can attach.
- **Threading:** a std listener thread (one client at a time) only moves text; each line goes over an mpsc channel to the UI thread with its own reply channel and wakes the idle winit loop (`EventLoopProxy`). No world access off the UI thread.
- **Same document, same History.** The UI thread answers in `State::drain_actions` after the user's own queued commands, through the existing `Server` dispatch (no tool code duplicated): the `Env` gets the GUI's world handle and borrows the GUI's own `History` for the call. An agent step is one Ctrl+Z, and the agent's `undo`/`redo` walk the user's steps too. Every call bumps `doc_version`; the status line reads `agent: <tool>`.
- **Status strip** shows `MCP listening on 127.0.0.1:<port>` while the server runs (default frames unchanged).
- **Never crash:** malformed JSON -> -32700; a dropped client, closed channel or >16 MiB line is logged and the listener carries on; dropping the `Inbox` stops and joins the thread (~50 ms) at shutdown.
- **Refused live:** `open_project` (would replace the user's document past the unsaved-changes prompt).
- New code: `crates/app/src/mcp/{listen,live,bridge}.rs`, `crates/ui/src/mcp_host.rs`; `mcp/tools.rs` and `mcp/edit.rs` untouched.

## Maintainer note (judgement call)
There is no authentication: any local process can drive the open document while the server is on. Being off by default and loopback-only is the guard; a token could be added later if wanted. `save_project` without a path saves over the open project but does not mark it clean, so the app may still ask to save. A long `generate` blocks the UI frame for its duration.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1722 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean. Hand run: `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7333` driven through `camcraft-cli mcp --connect` (set_stock, add_tool, add_operation all `isError:false`; `get_job` over nc showed the op in the app's world).

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/mcp_live.rs`: `a_live_call_lands_on_the_callers_history_and_its_undo_reverts_it`, `each_agent_step_is_one_undo_step_on_the_shared_history`, `the_live_session_refuses_open_project_and_reads_bad_lines_as_errors`, `the_port_flag_is_opt_in_and_checked`, `a_loopback_client_drives_the_owners_document_and_survives_bad_input` (real loopback TCP), `the_bridge_copies_stdio_to_a_live_session_and_back`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::mcp_live`: `an_agents_operation_shows_in_the_browser_and_ctrl_z_removes_it`, `the_status_strip_says_the_server_is_listening`.

## Not exercised
Ctrl+Z pressed by hand in the real window (harness only) - **draft until the GUI check**; Windows/Linux runs (std::net only); a real MCP client app beyond the bridge/nc; the bind-failure path (port in use). Posted G-code unchanged.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/183-mcp-live-gui.md`.

Changelog: The GUI can serve MCP live on a loopback port (`--mcp-port` / `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT`), so an agent's steps land in the open document and Ctrl+Z undoes them; `camcraft-cli mcp --connect` bridges stdio clients

Fixes #183

title: fix(post): judge the tool-number clash per machine
body:
**Replaces #440**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so #440 can no longer be updated. **Now stacked on #471** (the replacement for #439).

(Originally stacked on #439.) The #438 work is 9d9ac93d.

## What changed
- **The tool-number clash check (#221) is judged per machine.** `tool_numbers::clash_per_machine` runs the existing `clash()` on each machine group from `program_mounts(world, false)`. `posting::op_streams` calls it, which covers per-op files too.
- **Why per machine, not per NC file:** a T number names a pocket in one machine's tool changer.
  - Two machines have two tool tables, so T2 on each is fine.
  - Two posts on one machine still load from one carousel, so a shared number there is still refused.
  - Grouping per file (machine plus post) would let that real clash through, so I rejected it.
- **Messages:** a single-machine program gets the exact #221 message, unchanged. A multi-machine refusal starts with the mount's label (`Setup1 (machine, post): tools '…' and '…' would both post as T3 …`).
- The rationale is in `docs/decisions/388-per-setup-mount.md` (#438 section).

## How tested
- New `setup_mounts_post::a_tool_number_shared_across_machines_posts_but_clashes_within_one`:
  - across machines: a mill tool numbered 2 and the lathe's T2 post as two files;
  - within one machine: a clash is refused, naming both tools, the T number and Setup1, and not the lathe tool.
- `tool_numbers::two_tools_posting_one_number_refuse_by_name` (single machine) is unchanged and passes.
- `setup_mounts_post` 6/6, `setup_mount` 6/6, `tool_numbers` 6/6, `posting` 17/17, `post_not_judged` 4/4. `clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: The tool-number clash is judged per machine, so two machines in one program may each use the same T number (#438)

Fixes #438

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
**Stacked on #437** (#418), which is on #433 (#417) and #432 (#416). Until those merge, this diff includes their commits; the #419 work is 68bd14a5. Part of #363.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`

## How tested
- **New motion `turning_thread_dips`** (8 tests):
  - dips off lay the plain path bit for bit;
  - a dip is never deeper than its pass;
  - the phase is unchanged across the chain;
  - placement and slope rules hold;
  - a repeated depth cuts whole;
  - the verdict is silent on laid dips;
  - the verdict convicts each broken law (first/last lead, finishing pass, deeper, phase shift, steep). Temporarily disabling the laws made this test fail.
  - refusals by name.
- **New app `lathe_post_thread_dips`** (6 tests):
  - the golden `thread_g32_dips.nc`;
  - the posted chain keeps the plain thread's Z words and lead;
  - G76 refuses;
  - a post without `continuousThreading` refuses;
  - the lathe script refuses a bent dip;
  - dips ride the command, the stream and the project file.
- **Existing suites green:** the turning thread, infeed and G76 suites, `inverted_post`, `lathe_post*`, `project_roundtrip`, `conformance`, and all cl and post tests. No existing golden changed.
- `clippy -D warnings --all-targets` on motion, post, cl, app and ui is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **Machine check:** a run on a lathe simulator or machine.
- **GUI check:** the Passes-tab rows. The #416 test kit covers the neighbouring rows.

Changelog: Threading: optional in-pass chip-break dips on roughing passes, posted as continuous G32 X Z F segments by the Fanuc lathe post (#419)

Fixes #419
